Q: How to average multiple files across groups A:

After setting the input directory and reading in scang, try the following.

You say most samples were measured 2 or 3 times.
The auxiliary function fun starts by reading the 1st CSV file to know the data sets' dimensions. Then it creates an array with the same numbers of rows and columns and depth equal to length(infiles).
Then it loops through the remaining files, assigning in place each array layer the data.
Finally, it averages the layers and writes the result to outfile.

Untested, in the absence of data.

fun <- function(X) {
  infiles <- X[[2L]]
  outfile <- unique(X[[3L]])
  n <- length(infiles)
  dat1 <- read.csv(infiles[1L])
  arr <- array(dim = c(nrow(dat1), ncol(dat1), n))
  arr[,,1L] <- as.matrix(dat1)
  
  for(i in seq_along(infiles)[-1L]) {
    mat <- read.csv(infiles[i]) |> as.matrix()
    arr[,,i] <- mat
  }
  
  out <- if(n > 1L) {
    apply(arr, c(1L, 2L), mean) |> as.data.frame()
  } else dat1
  names(out) <- names(dat1)
  
  write.csv(out, outfile)
}

scan_split <- split(scang, scang$outname)
lapply(scang_split, fun)
